response.original_text: Many people think the most expensive decisions in life are buying a house, starting a business, or taking out a loan. They’re not. The most expensive decision you may ever make is your vote. Because one vote can influence the quality of education your children receive. The opportunities available to workers. The taxes you pay. The cost of living. The healthcare your family depends on. The laws that shape your everyday life. Yet every election season, some people vote based on popularity, catchy slogans, viral videos, family influence, or political loyalty. IMAGINE HIRING A MANAGER WITHOUT CHECKING THEIR QUALIFICATIONS. IMAGINE PROMOTING SOMEONE BECAUSE THEY’RE FAMOUS INSTEAD OF COMPETENT. No company would survive that. But somehow, we accept it when choosing leaders. A vote is not a gift to a politician. It is a responsibility to the people who will live with the consequences of that choice. Because sometimes, the price of a wrong vote is paid not for months but for years. I just hope that next time, we learn our lesson. That we stop treating elections like popularity contests and start treating them as decisions that shape the future of our nation. May we become wiser, more informed, and more responsible voters. Because the future we complain about tomorrow is often built by the choices we make today. Vote wisely. THE COUNTRY DESERVES BETTER AND SO DO WE.

Facebook Philippines observed that social media’s role “has become more critical than ever” when compared to the 2013 elections where “only about 30% of Filipinos had access to the Internet.” They said, “the proportion has grown dramatically since then.” From 25% of the population using the Internet in 2010, and 37% in 2013, it rose to an estimate of 42.3% in 2015, according to www.InternetLiveStats.com. But social media does not always have a good effect on candidates; since it is free, it can also backfire. citations.quote: This is just one example of the many campaign gimmicks political aspirants use to reach the public sphere, come election season.

From brand creation to troll armies, vloggers, and social media influencers, politicians have now understood the importance of using social media platforms, “whether to spread true campaigns or to spread disinformation.”

“Kailangan ngayon mag-compete in terms of how to get the public's attention. Kaya dito nag-aarise yung different gimmicks, different types of strategies online to get the public's attention,” Mendoza explained.

“Kasi kung lahat kayo, nasa social media, you need to strategize on how you will get [an] audience for your content. And in turn, ang nakikita natin is yung mga contents na need to be released ay mga emotionally charged, mga exaggerated na types of contents, kasi nga it would capture audiences more.”
Ang mas papansinin yun yung merong element ng galit, may element ng chismis, may element ng entertainment–which parang naging prominent strategy na ‘yun,” she continued.
This is evident in the prominence of celebrity political endorsers, celebrities-turned-politicians, and the practice of political celebrification.
Additionally, the study found that influencers have become a “highly attractive” tool for political campaigning due to their abilities to create spaces for refracted publics.
The campaign materials, such as hashtags, memes, fake news write-ups, and videos, are later disseminated through platforms like X (formerly Twitter) and Facebook.
Additionally, the study argued that digital influencers are also utilized, often to promote positive and personal branding that high-level strategists have created for their political clients.
As the 2025 midterm elections near, a variety of material continues to bombard people online, regardless of whether it's factual or not.
“Whether it's pro-administration or pro-opposition, that’s democracy. We can vote [for] whoever we want, as long as it's an educated choice and an informed choice,” she added.

content_profile.verification_text:
Many people think the most expensive decisions in life are buying a house, starting a business, or taking out a loan.
The most expensive decision you may ever make is your vote.
Because one vote can influence the quality of education your children receive.
The opportunities available to workers.
The healthcare your family depends on.
The laws that shape your everyday life.
Yet every election season, some people vote based on popularity, catchy slogans, viral videos, family influence, or political loyalty.
IMAGINE HIRING A MANAGER WITHOUT CHECKING THEIR QUALIFICATIONS.
IMAGINE PROMOTING SOMEONE BECAUSE THEY’RE FAMOUS INSTEAD OF COMPETENT.
No company would survive that.
But somehow, we accept it when choosing leaders.
A vote is not a gift to a politician.
It is a responsibility to the people who will live with the consequences of that choice.
Because sometimes, the price of a wrong vote is paid not for months but for years.
I just hope that next time, we learn our lesson.
That we stop treating elections like popularity contests and start treating them as decisions that shape the future of our nation.
May we become wiser, more informed, and more responsible voters.
Because the future we complain about tomorrow is often built by the choices we make today.
